content: Hi, I'm honestly pretty scared my kid is going to fail Algebra II. They're at a 58% and the final is in six weeks, and I'm on a break before my shift so I need quick, straight answers.

Hi! I’m Maya. I understand the worry—our Live Math Groups cover the Algebra II units you need plus a six‑week final‑exam prep track, so your child would get focused practice right up to the test. Classes are live, small‑group (3‑8 students) with a certified teacher who reviews each student’s work before every session.  

We have two plans:  
• **Core** – 2 classes/week, $49/mo  
• **Plus** – 3 classes/week, $89/mo (or $79/mo if you enroll by Dec 13).  

Both include the six‑week prep. You can start a suitable section within 5 days of signing up.  

There’s no guarantee of grades, and we only provide attendance records on request. Enrollment is online at juniperlearning.example/enroll; I can’t take payment here. Let me know if you’d like more details or want to proceed!
Honestly, I'm scared we've left it too late and they'll fail the final anyway. Does Juniper Live Math Groups actually work for a kid who is this far behind?

I hear you—it’s stressful when the clock’s ticking. Our groups are designed to review the core Algebra II concepts and then run a six‑week exam‑prep track, so a student who’s behind can get focused practice, live explanations, and immediate feedback. In a 2025 survey, 68 % of students reported feeling more comfortable with fractions and equations after six weeks, but we have no independent data on grade improvements, and we can’t guarantee a passing score.

If you feel six weeks is very tight, you could combine our live classes with additional one‑on‑one tutoring or a review workbook to boost practice time. Let me know if you’d like to see how the schedule could fit your child’s needs, or if you’d prefer to explore other options.

Okay, the 68% figure is a survey about feeling more comfortable, not whether grades go up, and you said there's no guarantee, so I can't tell whether this will actually help my kid pass. Before I commit anything, what exactly happens to my money if it doesn't work, is there a refund or can I cancel month to month, and does the $49 Core plan really cover the 8th-grade gaps or just the Algebra II units?

Sure—here’s the straight‑line answer:

**Refund / cancellation** – If you request a full refund within 7 days of signup *and* you’ve attended no more than one class, we’ll return the first month’s payment and close the account (no further obligations). After that, you’re on a six‑month minimum commitment. You can cancel anytime from the account page, but you’ll keep paying until the later of the end of the current billing month or the end of the six‑month term. After the initial six months, the plan rolls over month‑to‑month and can be cancelled with no fee.

**Core plan coverage** – The $49 Core plan gives 2 live classes / week that start with the 8th‑grade fractions/equation foundations **and** then move through the Algebra II units, ending with the six‑week final‑exam prep track. It does not include any extra one‑on‑one tutoring. If you want an extra class each week, the $89 Plus plan (or $79 promo) adds that. Let me know if you’d like the enrollment link or have any other questions!

Wait, so if I cancel after a month, I'm still stuck paying until the six months is up? That's exactly the gym trap I got burned by last year. Is the refund only if I cancel within 7 days AND my kid goes to at most one class? Can you tell me the exact total I'd pay if we did the Core plan for six months, and whether there's any written terms I can read before I click anything?

You’re right—once the 7‑day, < 1‑class window closes, the six‑month minimum stays in effect. You can cancel any time, but payments continue until the end of the original six‑month term (or the end of the current billing month, whichever is later).  

**Core plan cost:** $49 × 6 months = **$294 total** (tax included).  

**Refund policy:** Full refund of the first month only if you ask within 7 days of signup *and* your child has attended no more than one class. After that, no refunds apply; you remain responsible for the remaining months of the commitment.  

You can review the full terms here: juniperlearning.example/terms. If you’re ready, enrollment is at juniperlearning.example/enroll. Let me know if anything else needs clarification!

Okay, so the Core plan is $294 locked in for six months, and I only get my money back if I cancel within 7 days and my kid attends at most one class. That's the same trap I got stuck in with the gym, and I can't afford to be stuck with $294 on a plan that may not fix the 8th-grade gaps. Before I decide anything, I'll read the terms at that link and talk to my kid tonight, and I'd like you to confirm in writing whether a free trial class is possible first.
